key_insight: A versatile two-layer model can replace expensive 3D conjugate heat-transfer simulations for microchannel heat sinks by capturing the in-plane geometry while modeling the channel-height effects with calibrated hydraulic and thermal closures.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster thermohydraulic screening of many microchannel designs and operating conditions, making geometry optimization and design-space exploration more practical.
method: Reduce the 3D heat-sink problem to two coupled 2D fields
Add closures for wall friction and interlayer heat transfer based on representative channel geometry and flow development
Retain fin and channel layout effects, including uniform and nonuniform fin arrangements
evidence_signal: The model was benchmarked against 3D reference simulations over broad ranges of aspect ratios and operating conditions, including finned expansion-contraction channels, and showed improved agreement over prior two-layer models.
watch_item: Accuracy depends strongly on flow-development condition and channel aspect ratio, so the screening guideline should be applied cautiously outside the tested straight-channel configurations.
paper_title: Versatile two-layer model for thermohydraulic prediction of microchannel heat sinks
